data.title: npm
data.tagline: Install JavaScript packages and run project scripts
data.description: npm is a package manager and command runner for JavaScript projects. package.json records dependencies and named scripts, while the lockfile keeps installed versions reproducible. Install packages intentionally and review scripts before running code from an unfamiliar project.

use: Add a library to a project
Run scripts such as dev, test, and build
Keep dependency versions reproducible with a lockfile
avoid: Delete the lockfile whenever versions conflict
Install a package before checking whether the platform already provides the feature
Run an unfamiliar package script without reading it

lessonPractice.title: You just cloned a JavaScript project. It contains package.json and a lockfile but no node_modules. How should dependencies be restored?

options.label: Ask a teammate to zip their node_modules and copy it over the project
options.feedback: The dependency directory may differ by system and does not need manual transfer. The manifest and lockfile are the reproducible source.

options.label: Enter the project directory, run npm install, then use the project's defined scripts
options.feedback: npm restores dependencies from package.json and the lockfile so project scripts can use the intended tools.

options.label: Install every missing package globally until the startup errors disappear
options.feedback: Guessing global packages bypasses the project's locked versions and cannot reproduce the same environment elsewhere.

data.agentPrompt: Confirm that the current directory contains package.json and its lockfile, then restore dependencies with the project's existing package manager. Do not copy or edit node_modules or add arbitrary global packages. Run the existing dev or check script afterward and report the result.
